name: Hirokazu Sugiura
current_role: Founder and adviser (non-executive), Sugi Holdings; chairman of the council of the Sugiura Memorial Foundation
profile: Pharmacist Hirokazu Sugiura (b. 1950, Nishio, Aichi) founded Sugi Pharmacy in 1976 and built it into Sugi Holdings, one of Japan's largest drugstore/dispensing chains (~¥1 trillion revenue). He was president 1982-2009 and chairman until 2021, when his son Katsunori became president; he is now an adviser and focuses on the family's health foundation.
interesting_fact: The first Sugi Pharmacy was a 16-tsubo (about 53 m2) shop in Nishio, opened in December 1976 at the same time he married fellow Gifu Pharmaceutical University graduate Akiko, who became the company's co-founder and vice president.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 he and Akiko built the 'Nishio Citizens' Genki Plaza', a health-promotion centre on the site of the very first Sugi Pharmacy store, and lent the building and land to the city free of charge (opened April 2017).
notes: Name in input is misspelled 'Sugiara'; correct romanization is Sugiura (杉浦広一). Low public profile; Japanese-language outreach via the Sugiura Memorial Foundation is the most plausible route. Cited his reading favorites: Tempu Nakamura and Peter Drucker.

name: Xia Yibo
current_role: Non-executive director, Greentown Service Group (HKEX: 2869) (per market-data profiles; verify in latest annual report)
profile: Xia Yibo co-founded Hangzhou developer Greentown with her husband Song Weiping in 1994; it became one of China's best-known premium home builders (Greentown China, HKEX: 3900). The couple sold most of their Greentown China stake to China Communications Construction Group in 2014-15; her wealth now rests largely on a large holding in property-manager Greentown Service.
interesting_fact: Greentown was started in 1994 when Song Weiping, a former history teacher, returned to Hangzhou and founded the company together with Xia Yibo.
notes: Very private; almost no independent biography or interviews found. Wealth listed jointly with husband Song Weiping. No published personal/office contact; any approach would go through Greentown Service (Hangzhou) corporate channels.

name: Nikita Mishin
current_role: Founder, Dar Charitable Foundation for the Promotion of Education; private investor (former Globaltrans co-owner)
profile: Nikita Mishin (b. 1971) built his fortune in Russian freight logistics with partners Konstantin Nikolaev and Andrei Filatov, co-founding rail operator Globaltrans and port group Global Ports. He exited ports in 2017 and sold his Globaltrans stake around 2024; UK-based, he now devotes himself largely to education philanthropy through his Dar foundation.
interesting_fact: His Dar foundation opened Moscow's New School in 2017 with needs-blind admission and fees about half those of other private schools; it gets roughly 600 applicants for ~48 entry places a year.
deep_cut_fact: He studied philosophy at Moscow State University, earning a degree that qualified him to teach or research the subject, and has said: 'I was never absolutely happy being just an entrepreneur.' He reportedly still sits in on New School classes via Zoom.
notes: Best angle is education philanthropy (Dar / New School). Dar foundation is based in Moscow; he lives in the UK (dual UK citizenship since 2024 per Forbes). Wikipedia also notes Cypriot citizenship (2015).

name: René Holeček
current_role: Majority shareholder and Vice-chairman of the Supervisory Board, Colt CZ Group SE (per company corporate-affairs page)
profile: René Holeček (b. 1966), a Czech engineer-turned-banker, invested in ailing Česká zbrojovka Uherský Brod in 2001, took control in 2014 and listed it in Prague in 2020. He turned it into Colt CZ Group, buying US icon Colt (2021) and ammunition maker Sellier & Bellot (2024), and has since added an Amsterdam listing.
interesting_fact: Before guns he was a banker in the early 1990s (senior roles at Komerční banka and Pragobanka) and helped privatize the giant Třinec ironworks with long-time partner Rudolf Ovčaří.
deep_cut_fact: Forbes Czech lists his 'obsession' as golf, and with partner Rudolf Ovčaří he invested heavily in building golf courses and leisure resorts. His Holeček Family Foundation (Nadace rodiny Holečkových) funds education, health, science, crisis intervention and culture.
notes: Extremely low media profile (Forbes CZ calls him the 'mysterious owner'); rarely gives interviews. Best route is Colt CZ media relations. Defence/ammunition manufacturing angle may fit energy/industrial episodes.

name: Jerry Seinfeld
current_role: Stand-up comedian, writer and producer; co-creator of 'Seinfeld'; touring comic
profile: Jerry Seinfeld (b. 1954, raised in Massapequa, NY) co-created and starred in NBC's 'Seinfeld' (1989-98) with Larry David; his billionaire fortune comes mainly from his share of the show's syndication and streaming revenue plus touring. He still tours stand-up and has made Netflix specials, 'Comedians in Cars Getting Coffee', 'Bee Movie' and the 2024 film 'Unfrosted'.
interesting_fact: A serious car collector with about 150 cars, mostly Porsches; the centerpiece has been Steve McQueen's Porsche 917 (chassis 022) driven in the 1971 film 'Le Mans'.
deep_cut_fact: At 16 he volunteered on Kibbutz Sa'ar in Israel; he later started at SUNY Oswego before transferring to Queens College (BA communications and theater, 1976), doing open-mic nights at Budd Friedman's Improv while still a student. He has practiced Transcendental Meditation since about 1972.
notes: Celebrity; outreach realistically via his talent representation/publicist rather than direct. Car collecting and his long-form interview podcast appearances are natural hooks; not an energy/data-center figure.

name: Charles Cassius Gates Jr.
profile: Died August 28, 2005 (born May 27, 1921). He ran Denver's Gates Rubber Company/Gates Corporation from 1961, diversified it (including Learjet) and sold it to Tomkins plc in 1996; trustee emeritus of the Gates Family Foundation.
notes: Deceased (2005) per Wikipedia; skipped further research. Family philanthropy continues via the Gates Family Foundation (Colorado), gatesfamilyfoundation.org.

name: Ira Ehrenpreis
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, DBL Partners; independent director of Tesla and director of SpaceX (per Tesla IR and SEC insider filings)
profile: Ira Ehrenpreis is a Silicon Valley venture capitalist (since 1996) who led the energy-innovation practice at Technology Partners before co-founding impact-VC firm DBL Partners. An early Tesla and SpaceX backer and long-serving Tesla board member, his wealth derives largely from those stakes; he remains a prominent clean-energy investor and governance figure.
interesting_fact: He founded and chairs the World Energy Innovation Forum, which he staged inside Tesla's Fremont factory, with speakers such as Elon Musk, Lyndon Rive, Steven Chu and GE's Jeff Immelt.
deep_cut_fact: A UCLA Phi Beta Kappa/summa cum laude grad, he earned a joint JD/MBA at Stanford, where he was an associate editor of the Stanford Law Review; he was inducted into the International Green Industry Hall of Fame in 2014 and chaired the Silicon Valley Technology Innovation & Entrepreneurship Forum (2014-17).
notes: Strong fit for an energy/entrepreneurship podcast: clean-energy VC who runs the World Energy Innovation Forum. His DBL bio page publishes a direct work email. Tesla/SpaceX board seats make him media-cautious on those companies.

name: Lee Joong-keun
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Booyoung Group (co-led with chairman Lee Yong-seop since March 2026); president, Korea Senior Citizens Association and UN Association of Korea
profile: Lee Joong-keun (b. 1941), born to a farming family in Suncheon, founded Booyoung Group and is credited with popularising private rental housing in South Korea, building it into a major construction and property group with resorts. After legal troubles (pardoned in 2023) he returned to management and remains active in philanthropy.
interesting_fact: His Woojung Education and Culture Foundation funds scholarships for foreign students, in August 2026 awarding about ₩400 million to 98 students from 32 countries; he also chairs the Korea Senior Citizens Association and the UN Association of Korea.
deep_cut_fact: In 2023 he personally gave cash gifts of up to ₩100 million to about 280 households in his home village of Unpyeong-ri, Suncheon, and to his old classmates from Dongsan Elementary and Suncheon Middle School; residents said they 'thought it was a dream'.
notes: Age ~85. Forbes bio covers past criminal convictions and pardons; avoid in outreach. No published direct contact found; route via Booyoung Group corporate PR (Korean). Search budget ran out before a press email could be checked.

name: Irvine Laidlaw, Lord Laidlaw
current_role: Chairman, Irvine Laidlaw Foundation (Laidlaw Foundation); private investor
profile: Irvine Laidlaw (b. 1942, Keith, Banffshire) built the Institute for International Research from a small US publisher bought in 1973 into the world's largest conference organiser, selling it in 2005 for about £768m; he also founded Abbey Business Centres. A former Conservative life peer (2004-2010), he now focuses on education philanthropy via the Laidlaw Foundation.
interesting_fact: A keen historic racer, he owned and raced a Le Mans-winning 1950s Jaguar and a 1962 Ferrari 250 GTO before stopping racing in 2013. Wikipedia also says he part-owns a $2.1bn wind-farm project.
deep_cut_fact: His £9m gift to the University of Leeds, where he studied economics in the 1960s, was its largest ever and funded the £26m Laidlaw Library (opened 2015). His Laidlaw Scholarships for undergraduate research and leadership now run at about 19 universities including Oxford, Cambridge, Columbia and EPFL.
notes: Contacts are for his foundation, not him personally. Possible energy angle via reported wind-farm investment (unverified detail). Left the House of Lords in 2010.

name: Kunal Shah
current_role: Head of WhatsApp, Meta (since June 2026); founder of CRED (stepped down as CEO)
profile: Kunal Shah (b. 1979, Mumbai) co-founded recharge/payments app FreeCharge in 2010, sold it to Snapdeal in 2015 for roughly US$400m, then founded members-only credit-card rewards platform CRED and became one of India's most prolific angel investors (200+ deals). In June 2026 Meta named him head of WhatsApp, succeeding Will Cathcart, while investing $900m in CRED for ~20%.
interesting_fact: Mark Zuckerberg hired him to run WhatsApp, the world's biggest messaging app, saying he 'built CRED into one of India's most important technology companies'; Meta simultaneously took a ~20% stake in CRED for $900m.
deep_cut_fact: He studied philosophy at Wilson College, Mumbai, worked from his teens, and dropped out of a part-time MBA at NMIMS in 2004; FreeCharge grew out of a pivot of his earlier cashback start-up PaisaBack (2009). ET named him 'Comeback Kid of the Year' in 2016.
notes: Very active on X (@kunalb11) where he posts frequently on consumer behaviour and India; now a senior Meta executive so interview requests likely go via Meta/WhatsApp comms. X handle is widely known but source here is the account itself.

name: Namit Malhotra
current_role: CEO of DNEG; founder and non-executive chairman of Prime Focus Ltd; film producer (Ramayana)
profile: Namit Malhotra (b. 1976, Mumbai), from a film family, started an editing studio in 1995 that became Prime Focus (listed 2006). He expanded globally, pioneered 3D conversion and in 2014 merged Prime Focus World with London's Double Negative to form DNEG, the multi-Oscar-winning VFX studio behind Interstellar, Tenet and Dune. He also produces films, including the big-budget 'Ramayana' (2026).
interesting_fact: DNEG, which he leads, has won Academy Awards for Best Visual Effects for films including Inception, Interstellar, Ex Machina, Blade Runner 2049, First Man, Tenet, Dune and Dune: Part Two.
deep_cut_fact: He launched his first business, Video Workshop, in his father's garage in 1995 after a computer-graphics course, recruiting three of his own teachers as co-founders. His grandfather, cinematographer M. N. Malhotra, shot one of India's first colour films, 'Jhansi Ki Rani' (1953).
notes: High-profile in Indian and Hollywood media; currently promoting Ramayana. DNEG PR is the best route. Data-center angle: VFX rendering is compute-heavy (DNEG runs large render farms).

name: Ruth Parasol
current_role: Principal benefactor and trustee director, Parasol Foundation Trust (Gibraltar)
profile: Ruth Parasol (b. 1967, San Francisco), a lawyer by training, founded the business that became PartyGaming in 1997; after PartyPoker's launch it floated in London in 2005 at about $8.5bn and entered the FTSE 100. She sold her last shares in 2015 and, based mainly in Gibraltar, now focuses on philanthropy through the Parasol Foundation Trust.
interesting_fact: PartyGaming's 2005 float made it, per Wikipedia, the first female-founded and -led company admitted to the FTSE 100.
deep_cut_fact: Her Parasol Foundation funds a scholarship programme at Murray Edwards College, Cambridge, for talented female students to study astronomy, and gave $3.5m to create a women's breast cancer centre at Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center; the trust has given over £40m since 2004, focused on women in STEM and health.
notes: Private; best approach is via the Parasol Foundation (women in STEM / tech pioneer angle). Avoid PartyGaming legal history and earlier adult-industry businesses in outreach.

name: Richard Farmer
profile: Richard T. Farmer (Nov 22, 1934 - Aug 4, 2021), founder and long-time CEO/chairman of uniform company Cintas, died in 2021 aged 86.
notes: Deceased (August 2021) per Wikipedia; skipped further research. Legacy: Farmer School of Business at Miami University (Ohio).

name: Patricia Matte
current_role: Honorary councillor, Sociedad de Instrucción Primaria (SIP Red de Colegios); member of the Matte family (CMPC shareholders)
profile: Patricia Matte Larraín (b. 1943, Santiago) is the eldest child of industrialist Eliodoro Matte Ossa and shares in the Matte family fortune built on forestry/paper giant Empresas CMPC. A sociologist (Universidad Católica, 1969), she worked on social and anti-poverty policy and later concentrated on education through the SIP network of free schools.
interesting_fact: She focused much of her career on the Sociedad de Instrucción Primaria, a Chilean network of tuition-free schools founded in 1856 that celebrated 170 years in 2026; she now sits on its council of honorary members.
deep_cut_fact: A trained sociologist, she started her career at the UN's Economic Commission for Latin America (CEPAL) and later helped design poverty-reduction programmes at the national planning office (Odeplan); she received Chile's Premio Bicentenario in 2007.
notes: Low profile, ~83 years old; wealth is shared family wealth (CMPC). Her role in the Pinochet-era government is politically sensitive; avoid in outreach. SIP communications is the only published channel found.

name: Lu Rongfu
current_role: Co-founder and deputy general manager, Xiamen Yealink Network Technology (SZSE: 300628) (per Forbes; not re-verified for 2026)
profile: Lu Rongfu co-founded the predecessor of Xiamen-based Yealink in 2001 with Chen Zhisong, Zhou Jiwei and Wu Zhongyi. Yealink grew from OEM USB and SIP phones into its own brand of IP desk phones and video-conferencing systems, listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2017; his fortune comes from his Yealink shareholding.
interesting_fact: Yealink started out making USB phones as an OEM (2001-05), moved into SIP/VoIP handsets, dropped OEM work in 2011 to build its own brand, and in 2018 became a Microsoft strategic partner, co-developing Microsoft Teams desk phones.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal interviews found. Contacts are corporate Yealink channels. Web-search budget was exhausted, so current title not re-verified against latest filings.

name: Qin Hua
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Gambol Pet Group (SZSE-listed), Liaocheng, Shandong
profile: Qin Hua is chairman and CEO of Gambol Pet Group, a pet-food maker founded in 2006 in Liaocheng, Shandong, that grew from OEM/ODM exports into one of China's leading pet-food companies. He became a billionaire when Gambol listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in August 2023; KKR is among its investors.
interesting_fact: Gambol now runs 3 R&D centres and 25 factories across China, Thailand and New Zealand, with 1,300+ products exported to more than 30 countries in Europe, the U.S., Japan and South Korea.
notes: Low international profile; Chinese-language outreach via Gambol's board office/IR (Shenzhen filings) would be the realistic route. The gambolpet.com site is the OEM/export arm (published email brand@gambolpet.com is a sales inbox). Web-search budget exhausted before a deep-cut fact could be sourced.

name: Wu Peifu
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu Shuangxing Color Plastic New Materials Co. (SZSE: 002585), Suqian, Jiangsu (per Forbes)
profile: Wu Peifu (about 65 per Forbes 2022) founded and chairs Jiangsu Shuangxing Color Plastic New Materials, founded in 1997 in Suqian and listed in Shenzhen in 2011. Starting in packaging film, it has become a major Chinese maker of polyester functional films, including optical films (a Samsung VD supplier since 2019), new-energy materials and energy-saving window films; the wealth is held with his family.
interesting_fact: The 'Chairman's message' on Shuangxing's website sets out a personal creed: 'do one practical thing a day, one new thing a month, one big thing a year, and one meaningful thing in a lifetime.'
notes: Forbes bio misspells him 'Wang Peifu'; not to be confused with warlord Wu Peifu (1874-1939). Company name is Shuangxing ('Shuangxin' in input). New-energy films offer an energy angle. Very low public profile; Chinese-language outreach via company/IR office. Web-search budget exhausted before a deep-cut fact could be sourced; the motto is from the chairman's page and not explicitly signed by him.

name: Yu Jiqun
current_role: Reported co-founder/controlling shareholder (with wife Cao Peifeng) of Yongjin Technology Group (formerly Zhejiang Yongjin Metal Technology, SSE: 603995); current title not verified
profile: Yu Jiqun is listed by Hurun with Cao Peifeng as the founders behind Yongjin, a Lanxi, Zhejiang-based cold-rolled stainless-steel group founded in August 2003. It now has 10 production bases (including Vietnam) with 4m+ tonnes of annual capacity and has diversified into titanium alloys, stainless water pipes and battery-casing materials for new-energy vehicles.
interesting_fact: Yongjin ranked 211th among China's top 500 private manufacturers in 2025 and makes ultra-precise stainless strip as thin as 0.04 mm on twenty-high reversing cold mills, including lines it designed itself.
